newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha firmer on crudes, spreads unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha firmer on crudes, spreads unchanged.

text.p: Near-term naphtha prices climbed back above the $230 level on Thursday, the first time this month, buoyed by firmer overnight crude prices, traders said.
"It's mostly crude gains, but bullish fundamentals also gave support to naphtha levels," one trader said.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half May was quoted at $230.00/232.00 per tonne, up from Wednesday's $228.50/230.00.
Second-half May was assessed at $226.50/228.50. It was traded at $226.25 between European traders on Wednesday.
The one-month spread from first-half May was discussed little changed from Wednesday at plus $5.50/6.50.
Second-half May/second-half June was quoted at $4.50/5.50.
In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, offers for prompt Indonesian cargoes were nominally assessed at 40 to 50 cents over the Pertamina formula.
About 1.2 million barrels of Indonesian cargoes were believed to have been destined for Japan for March, compared to 1.6 to two million barrels for February, traders said.
The decline in Japan's spot LSWR imports in March was attributed to slow demand from electric utilities amid mild weather, traders said.
